observations: Lively laughing adult, bent planted stance and bulging ram eyes give strong impact appeal.

Prior chip is not clearly retained on the crescent glove. Structural retry is justified by side/cheek consequence; not a cosmetic preference.
Grounded backward lean, boot tracks and awkward crossed ram forelegs convey opposed recoil without duplicated obvious limbs. Correct RIGHT circle/LEFT crescent restored.
Crescent edge appears largely intact; chip continuity remains weak. Cheeks remain full round balls rather than visibly deflated.
Bright adult joy and indignant ram personality remain strong; busy chalk chips, grass and wool patches warrant selective finishing.
Breathless laughing seated adult and sulky resting ram provide a charming emotional payoff. Crescent LEFT is visibly worn/chipped now, RIGHT circle intact and no charge.

Warm rounded painting style and substantial adult build persist; ground/grass/wool density remains high.

native_exposure: Parent said ST06 structural punch/compression retry had been allocated before these three views. No returned repair verdict or root ledger read.
phone_observations: Personally inspected actual full uncaptioned ST8 strip and both NG06 P/R1 phone histories.

ST broad sequence is readable: charge, enemy mouth blast, airborne shock, landing, safe flank recharge, counterpunch, recoil and comic recovery. This is the strongest broad emotional/cause-response arc of the three primaries, not proof of every power rule.

At phone size ST03 blast source and suspended body remain distinct; ST06 counter is identifiable but cheek compression is weak, equipment sides reverse and chip does not persist reliably. Bright field/wool/ground patches remain everywhere.
NG06-R1 phone clearly restores one cyan pull line and removes second sword. Prefer R1 qualified; attacking LEFT remains wrong, and no second repair is allowed.

recommendations.final_two_repairs: NG03 plus ST06 is defensible after whole-set review: both target decisive power beats. Earlier BP02 alternative remains documented, and its closed-petal/root timing failure must stay visible.
